public_rationale: NewsGuard's tracker of unreliable AI-generated news sites rose from just under 50 in May 2023 to about 600 in December 2023, then to 713 by February 22, 2024. That is more than a tenfold rise in under a year. On April 4, 2024, two days before the post, X promoted a false headline written by its Grok chatbot to its whole user base. Mashable called that a first for the platform. Together these show the problem was growing quickly when he wrote.
limitations: Tracker counts come from one commercial source and may partly reflect more searching rather than only more sites.
Counts of sites are not the same as reach or harm.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative-AI pollution of the information ecosystem is getting worse quickly as of April 2024.

statement.excerpt: The bad news, which outweighs the good, is that the problem is quickly getting worse.

our_interpretation: 'The problem' is generative-AI pollution of the information ecosystem: AI-made false or junk content reaching the public.
Plain reading: measurable signs of this pollution rose fast in the months before the post.
Period chosen: May 2023 (when trackers began counting) to the post date. This is the most recent stretch public evidence could cover before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Trackers or documented incidents show AI-generated misinformation sources or incidents growing quickly between mid-2023 and early April 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Trackers show flat or falling counts of AI misinformation sources or incidents over that period.

evidence.excerpt: a rise in AI-generated sites making false or unverified claims from just under 50 in May to around 600 in December 2023, a more than tenfold increase across just over half a year.
evidence.explanation: A more than tenfold rise in AI content-farm sites in about seven months is fast growth in AI information pollution.

evidence.excerpt: The number of websites using AI-generated content to spread fake news has increased to 713 as of February 22
evidence.explanation: The count was still climbing in February 2024, about six weeks before the post.

evidence.excerpt: the first time X took Grok's misinformation, packaged it as a real trending news story, and promoted it to its entire user base
evidence.locator: section 'The danger of X depending on AI', near end
evidence.explanation: A new, platform-wide channel for AI-made false news appeared two days before the post, a further sign that the problem was escalating.
